goal_title: Book: Swarm Intelligence: Where Coordination Lives — improvements from the spine reading
why: The whole spine was read as a book on 2026-09-24, one sequence at a time, and every stumble, false claim or broken handover in swarmintelligence became a task Palle can pick up one at a time. Reader: the VR visitor.
success_criteria: every open task here is done or skipped with a note
the chapters read through without a stumble in the headset
every code excerpt and number in the chapters matches the source

book.title: Swarm Intelligence: Where Coordination Lives
chapters_read: Boolean_Works (last of boolean_surfaces, for the handover in)
ML_Evolution (first of machinelearning, for the handover out)

reading.arc: The sequence asks one question seven ways: when many bodies move together, what supplied the coordination? Physarum puts the memory in the ground; Flow Fields hands the ground a set of directions from outside; Boids removes the ground and makes neighbours the moving reference; the ABM hall gives agents state and a field that forgets at a rate the visitor sets; the ant colony splits the trail into a home channel and a food channel; the particle swarm moves memory inside the agent as a scored position; and the ecosystem adds a caretaker at population scale whose interventions are printed beside the box. Every chapter follows the same shape - watch one thing, the mechanism in plain words, what the picture cannot prove, a deferred experiment, a one-line handover - and every caveat re-says the sequence truth, that collective movement does not identify its cause. The arc lands cleanly on machine learning: inherited traits, environmental reward, and the rules that keep the experiment running.
holds: The refrain 'who or what supplied this': a field written versus a field given (Physarum/FlowFields), remembered visits versus remembered evaluations (ants/PSO), local events versus a caretaker (ecosystem) - each chapter re-asks the sequence truth in its own terms.

A one-line handover closing every chapter that names the next room's change of source: supplied direction -> neighbours -> internal state and a remembering environment -> two channels -> scored memory -> quieter rules that keep a system alive.

The 'watch the fading route, not the strong one' device: Physarum's abandoned path, FlowFields' surprising arrow, ABM's persistence versus width, ACO's less-reinforced food direction, PSO's place that was bright and is no longer.

Explicit back-references that chain the halls: FlowFields names Physarum; ACO names 'the previous room'; PSO names 'the ant colony's traces'; the capstone recaps 'A flock followed neighbours; ants read traces; particles pursued remembered scores.'

Repeatable beginnings as a method: RESET restores the same food, qualities and headings in the ant hall, and the same scatter and velocities in the swarm hall, so 'change one thing' can mean something.
One identical skeleton per chapter: H1, a one-line question, a single anchored work, eight to ten short paragraphs of roughly 400-570 words, a deferred experiment, the handover.

hall_notes.note: Opens on environmental memory: follow one bright connection through the twenty-second carousel of anchor layouts, then a junction, then the route that is fading. Reads as a patient watching instruction with the mechanism (sense ahead and to the sides, deposit, spread, decay, anchors emitting) given once in plain words; the organism the colony is named after is never named in the text.

The supplied field: predict an agent's turn from its arrow through the ten-second tour that ends parked in noise, with two small checks (same patch, different histories; near arrows, opposite directions). The cost-map paragraph and 'a field can give a direction without giving a destination' are the sequence's clearest mechanism prose; the closing 'future version' defers an axis the code already has.

One slider at a time on the highlighted boid's three arrows, then RADIUS with the weights held; the turn to 'who can each agent perceive' and 'alignment is not consent' carry the critical weight. It addresses one of the hall's five flocks and never mentions the other four.

The most experimental chapter: RESET as a repeatable beginning, EVAPORATE as how fast the ground forgets, ANTS as replacing the population while leaving its field, then RESET again to erase the marks. Reads well as a protocol; the map's catalyst foe, vent and prompter box are absent from the text, and the three MODE behaviours are counted but not named.

Two channels: outward ants seek food and leave home, returning ants the reverse; a destination is a state change rather than a bright place. Names stigmergy, refuses the optimisation claim the map title invites, and is the cleanest self-contained chapter of the seven.

The longest chapter: CONVERGE, SPREAD and NOVELTY as three scores put to the same bodies, the archive of two hundred, re-scoring memories, inertia. The strongest argument in the sequence ('Best is a relation between a position and an objective'), but the console's fourth button is missing from the text and the length shows in the second half.

The capstone: alternate scale between one encounter and the count, then read the POPULATION SUPPORT record beside the box and look back at the organisms. Recaps the sequence in one line, lands the truth - name the support before calling a thing self-organising - and hands over to machine learning without strain.

stumbles: SwarmIntelligence_PhysarumColony: 'a biological name does not make these simulated agents an experimental account of an organism' - but no biological name has been given; the reader has only the in-world caption PHYSARUM and the next chapter's 'Physarum's agents' as if it had been introduced.

SwarmIntelligence_PhysarumColony: 'The earlier emergence rooms asked how repeated local updates produce a pattern' reaches back to cellular automata, seven sequences earlier, while the reader has just left Boolean Works carrying 'the question of accommodation' that nothing here picks up.

SwarmIntelligence_FlowFields: 'Where the direction is zero, the agents have a wandering behaviour' sits in the wind-and-noise paragraph, but wind and noise fill every cell; the zero vector belongs to the target cell and to sealed cells in the route-finding scenes.

SwarmIntelligence_FlowFields: 'For a future version, hiding the arrows while holding the scene fixed...' - the artifact already has a field_display:hidden axis and a pinnable scenario, so the sequence's sharpest test of its own thesis is deferred rather than staged.

SwarmIntelligence_FlowFields: the 50 m ant terrain and the ecosystem box - the primary works of chapters five and seven - stand three cells from the field, unmentioned, and are met again later as if new.

SwarmIntelligence_Boids_Algorithm: the hall has five flocks and a science screen; the chapter serves one. The flock that parts around the controller hand is the only place in the sequence where the visitor's body is a neighbour, and it is never mentioned. RESET here deals a fresh unseeded scatter, unlike the two seeded resets the reader is taught to rely on next.

SwarmIntelligence_Agent_Based_Modeling_ABM: 'Watch the colony long enough to recognise a trail' is written for an undisturbed hall, but the map places a catalyst_foe with the base 'foe' personality (chases, 15 contact damage), a vent, and a prompter box that opens two cells from the spawn.

SwarmIntelligence_Particle_Swarm_Optimization: 'These are three different questions put to the same moving bodies' - the console the visitor stands at has four buttons; RIDGE ('Meritocratic - One narrow path counts') is never mentioned.

SwarmIntelligence_Particle_Swarm_Optimization: 'continuing velocity and remembered positions can still influence where the next update carries the particle' - a landscape switch resets every remembered best to the present position, so only the velocity is carried across the switch the reader is told to watch.

Sequence-wide: all seven chapters end on a deferred experiment ('a proposal for this room's development', 'for a future version', 'a future experiment', 'a proposed extension', 'a useful future interaction', 'a future comparison' twice); by the fifth the book reads as a backlog, and the ACO deferral repeats Physarum's almost word for word.

keep.quote: There is no little map hidden inside the moving dots. Information persists outside them, in a medium that changes what later movements are likely to do.
A field can give a direction without giving a destination.
Shared navigation can reproduce those decisions very efficiently. Efficiency alone cannot tell us whether every traveller can use the permitted route.
Alignment is not consent, and cohesion is not a complete account of belonging. These agents have no way to refuse a relation, remember harm or ask another agent for space.
Replacing the travellers and erasing their history are two different acts.
A destination is more than a bright place to reach: arriving there changes what information that ant will seek and leave on the next stretch.
Yesterday's high score cannot simply win against today's distances: the question has changed under it. The particle retains a place, but its claim to be best has to be renewed.
That comparison need not make intervention shameful. Care, repair and replenishment can be necessary. The question is whether they remain visible when someone describes the result as autonomous.

reading.handover_in: Boolean_Works ends: 'In Swarm Intelligence, many bodies will follow local rules at once. Their movements will make relations that no single body can supply. Carry the question of accommodation with you: what space becomes possible among them?' Physarum opens 'Can a path remember where to grow when no individual carries a map?' The 'many bodies, local rules' promise is kept in substance by five hundred agents, but 'accommodation' is never picked up, and the chapter's only backward look is to 'the earlier emergence rooms' (cellular automata, spine position 12) rather than to the hall the reader just left (boolean_surfaces, 18). Serviceable, not stitched.
reading.handover_out: The capstone ends: 'Machine learning begins by asking what changes across generations. Carry this distinction with you: inherited traits, environmental rewards and the rules that keep an experiment running all shape what can survive.' ML_Evolution answers it directly in its mechanism paragraph - 'The ecosystem in the previous room combined local behaviour with balancing interventions. Here the lesson is to look carefully at the apparently ordinary rule that pays for survival' - and its title 'Survival without a finish line' is the same distinction one room on. This is the strongest seam in the sequence.

tasks.title: Account for the console's fourth button, RIDGE
tasks.spec:
[encounter] SwarmIntelligence_Particle_Swarm_Optimization
Quote: “These are three different questions put to the same moving bodies. The labels Corporate, Ecological and Artistic are invitations to argue about those questions”
Why: The physical console the visitor stands at offers four choices; the fourth, RIDGE (labelled 'Meritocratic - One narrow path counts'), is never mentioned, so a reader who presses it has left the chapter. It is also the sharpest case of the chapter's own point: one diagonal counts and everything else is dark.
Do: Change 'three' to 'four' and add a short paragraph after the NOVELTY passage: RIDGE scores perpendicular distance from the diagonal, so two particles far apart on the line score alike while one a hand's width off it scores as badly as one at the corner; 'Meritocratic' is the fourth invitation to argue. The closing line about displaying two conflicting scores can then name it.

tasks.title: Say what the three MODE behaviours are
tasks.spec:
[prose] SwarmIntelligence_Agent_Based_Modeling_ABM
Quote: “The MODE control offers three behaviours within this model family. It does not turn the room into a language for inventing arbitrary agents.”
Why: The reader is told the count and the caveat but not the behaviours, so pressing MODE is a guess; the label reads 'Mode: Colony / Communication / Multi-Source' and each changes what is drawn. The chapter's own rule - 'begin by naming exactly which rule or condition has changed' - goes unfollowed for its own control.
Do: One sentence: Colony is the foraging you have been watching; Communication lets an ant returning with good food send a ring out from the nest and lead one idle ant to the source in tandem; Multi-Source nudges foragers towards richer food and draws each source's quality as a ring around it.
